Rivers State Governor, Siminalayi Fubara, has said any of his supporters who refuse to join him in the Rainbow Coalition are on their own, insisting that his decision to return to his political family is non-negotiable. Fubara stated this on Thursday during the inauguration of the Rivers State All Progressives Congress Campaign Council Rainbow Coalition in Port Harcourt. Congratulating members whose names appeared on the list, the governor urged those who were omitted not to be discouraged, saying there were still sub-committees to be constituted and that the list could be updated. He, however, warned against divided loyalty. “We still have sub-committees. The list can also be updated, so you don’t have any problems to worry about. The most important thing is to work with your heart sincerely. “Don’t openly say you’re with me and behold you’re doing a different thing. I’m here, and I say it boldly anywhere, any day. And anybody who says he is not with me, gently go your way,” he said. Make PUNCH part of your everyday experience. Add us to your Preferred Sources He acknowledged that the new political reality following the prolonged crisis in the state might be difficult to accept but urged his supporters to put the past behind them and look to the future with optimism. “Don’t go behind and say this is Fubara, no, no, no. I have said it. It might be difficult, but we have gone past that. We are looking at the future and what God holds for us,” the governor added. Fubara charged members of the campaign team to work together to achieve their goals, expressing confidence that the coalition’s candidates would emerge victorious with the strategies in place. He said, “Nothing is impossible. Provided it’s something that has to do with life, it is possible. If we take it as a serious responsibility, a serious task that must be achieved, we will come out with a stronger vote than what we did in 2023. “It is only for us to say yes; we want to do it. And I’m very sure that with the strategy for the forthcoming elections, we are going to come out with good results, better than what we had before.” Edo’ll get more federal projects, Shettima assures residents FG to unveil export digital platform December 14 APC, NDC trade blame over Lagos town hall attack The governor thanked the Coordinator of the Presidential Campaign Council in Rivers State and Minister of the Federal Capital Territory, Chief Nyesom Wike, and other leaders for their efforts in establishing the council. Earlier, while inaugurating the campaign council, Wike said another campaign council would soon be inaugurated across the state’s 23 local government areas. He said the campaign would adopt a different approach, including reaching out to family meetings and age-grade groups to engage voters who had not been reached in previous campaigns. The minister said, “We are going away from that ceremonial campaign style. When we are going to Gokana today, we just stay in one field and begin to talk to those we already know. “It is going to be different. This time around, we are going round to communities, to family meetings, to age-grade meetings and other informal groups to talk to people, not necessarily those we meet with every day. “You and I, we meet every day, then tomorrow again we gather in one place and say we are holding a rally. We must depart from that.” Wike commended Fubara for attending the ceremony and other engagements of the council despite his busy schedule. The FCT minister, who is also the National Leader of the PDP/Rainbow Coalition, reminded members of the newly inaugurated Presidential Campaign Council that they had been selected based on their capacity to participate in the group’s activities and deliver results. He charged them to work hard to secure votes for the APC and Rainbow Coalition candidates in next year’s presidential, governorship, National Assembly and state House of Assembly elections. Wike added that, apart from the Presidential Campaign Council and its sub-committees, local government campaign councils would soon be inaugurated to ensure wider grassroots coverage.
